We now define the family of disjoint groups G = { g 1 , g 2 , g 3 } G=\{g_{1},g_{2},g_{3}\} used for the lower bound. The groups are designed to create a dilemma for the forecaster: deviating from honest predictions is detected by g 1 g_{1} and g 2 g_{2} , while staying honest exposes the forecaster to noise accumulation on g 3 g_{3} . Let η > 0 \eta>0 be a threshold parameter (to be chosen later): g 1 g_{1} is active on rounds where the prediction overshoots the context by at least η \eta ; g 2 g_{2} is active on rounds where the prediction undershoots by at least η \eta ; g 3 g_{3} is active on rounds where the prediction is η \eta -close to the context. η \eta will be set equal to δ ​ m T \delta\sqrt{\frac{m}{T}} , for a carefully selected constant δ \delta . The main technical tool we need is a lower bound on the deviation of a “filtered” martingale. When analyzing the η \eta -honest rounds (group g 3 g_{3} ), we must show that the noise terms Z t = x t − y t Z_{t}=x^{t}-y^{t} accumulate to large magnitude even when summed only over an adaptively-chosen subset of rounds.
